caveats: The publication-disabled simulated-Actions build-core run and the independent native-local build-core run reproduced the flycast_libretro.zip package, resolver metadata, both ABI artifacts, and both active-marker build logs byte for byte. Execution was local; both builds cloned the pinned source over the network, so no offline source cache is proven.

This is static build/package evidence only. ARM64 is build-identity-bound to ra64-universal-v1 and ARMHF to ra32-a30-v1. ARMHF requires GLIBCXX_3.4.32, above the observed non-enforcing Miyoo Mini fallback provider value GLIBCXX_3.4.24, so the Mini profile is ineligible; A30 is the eligible 32-bit consumer at the ABI screen. Provider inspection and target-runtime capture are absent, so every execution profile and device view remains provisional and ineligible pending a runtime smoke result.

Content, BIOS/firmware handling, controls, audio/video pacing, saves and state round trips, reset and unload behavior, frontend integration, compatibility, licensing review, and sustained performance remain target-runtime and human gates. Publication remains disabled regardless of local byte reproducibility.

The publication-disabled simulated-Actions build-core run and independent native-local build-core run reproduced the package, resolver metadata, both ABI artifacts, and both ABI build logs byte for byte. Both profiles used the generic direct-cmake proof; there is no per-core log contract.

The pristine source is tag v2.6, commit 392a429e8b040b3e5bf6696cb4f984274fc44123, tree 712e00d5a9c99abc949bcce2bf02800492de869d, with 25 recursive submodules pinned transitively by the tree. SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is pinned to 1767792512 (2026-01-07T13:28:32Z).

The reviewed configure set is LIBRETRO=ON, CMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=TRUE, USE_VULKAN=OFF, USE_HOST_LIBZIP=OFF, USE_OPENMP=OFF, with per-architecture GLES selection: USE_GLES (GLES3) on arm64 and USE_GLES2 on armhf. OpenMP is disabled because no device capture proves libgomp; Vulkan is disabled as no target device provides it.

One reviewed armhf overlay guards the vendored lzma HWCAP2_* names inside the core/deps/libchdr submodule: the A30 sysroot's older UAPI headers predate them, and a zero mask makes the runtime CPU-feature check report unsupported without forcing features. This is the first submodule-owned overlay; it applies from the submodule checkout and is verified against the submodule's own diff.

The arm64 artifact links no GL library (GL resolves at runtime through the frontend), unlike the shipped build. The armhf artifact links unversioned libGLESv2.so directly: the Mini family has no GLES2 provider, so its device views must report missing_provider; the A30 provides an unversioned GLES soname. GPU rendering requires a real GLES driver at runtime on every device.

Dreamcast/Naomi/Atomiswave content, BIOS discovery, dynarec correctness, save/state behavior, GPU-provider capture, performance, and licensing review remain target-runtime and human gates. flycast has no software rasterizer; device eligibility beyond loader truth requires GPU evidence. Publication remains disabled.
